ShortDescription.Value: Plop any vanilla zoned building as a property-free scenery piece. Lot surfaces and randomized decorations (trees, benches, planters, bins) come with it, exactly like the game does it.

Publish.LongDescription:
# Static Scenery Ploppables
Turn **any** vanilla zoned building into a **static, property-free scenery piece** you can place anywhere - no zoning requirements, no simulation load.
## What it does
- Browse all 2000+ vanilla zoned buildings in a Find It-style panel (search, zone tabs, filters for density / level / width / depth). - Click an entry and place it. The building is placed **with its vanilla lot surface and its randomized surroundings** - trees, benches, planters, bins, poles. - Every placement rolls its own decoration variant using the game's own randomization, so no two placements are identical. - The result is a pure shell: **no residents, no jobs, no households, no companies, no simulation cost**.
## Typical uses
- Decorate districts with buildings the zoning system would never allow. - Build back-lot scenery, alley filler, industrial parks, waterfront clutter. - Keep a city's look while freeing the lots from simulation.
## Compatibility and safety
- Decorations are placed **once**, at placement time. If a decoration prefab is missing in your city (e.g. DLC you do not own), it is simply skipped. - Relocation (the vanilla relocate tool) and bulldozing clean up the lot surfaces correctly. - Removing the mod is safe: the save still loads and does not crash. Placed scenery objects become missing-prefab placeholders (white models); bulldozing a placeholder removes its decorations too. Bulldoze your placed scenery before uninstalling if you want a clean map. - No dependencies on other mods. Works alongside Find It, Move It, Anarchy and ctrlC.
## Localization
Panel text follows your game language: English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Deutsch, Francais, Espanol, Portugues (BR), Russian, Polski, Japanese, Korean. Other languages fall back to English.
## Credits
Implementation learned from these open-source mods and community docs (approach reference only, no bundled code):
- Find It (JadHajjar) - panel UX and the `ToolSystem.ActivatePrefabTool` placement path: https://github.com/JadHajjar/FindIt-CSII - ctrlC (jk1422) - asset-stamp area copying and toolbar entry pattern: https://github.com/jk1422/ctrlC - Move It (Quboid) - project and build/deploy layout conventions: https://github.com/Quboid/CS2-MoveIt - Better Bulldozer (yenyang) - safe removal of building-owned sub-elements (`DeleteInXFrames` plus barrier `Deleted`): https://github.com/yenyang/BetterBulldozer - Plop the Growables (algernon-A) - confirmation that CS2 supports placing growables directly, which led to dropping asset stamps: https://github.com/algernon-A/PlopTheGrowables - cs2-modding-guide (BrokeAssSoftware) - verified rules for sub-element removal: https://github.com/BrokeAssSoftware/cs2-modding-guide - Cities Skylines 2 Modding Guide (ps1ke) - API reference: https://ps1ke.github.io/Cities-Skylines-2-Modding-Guide/
Source code: https://github.com/LiangHaoXiang/StaticSceneryPloppables
